questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The choice of my destination was partly because I love Berlin and its openness. It is its own thing from the rest of Germany. Furthermore, I work in a law office in Copenhagen that works with a German insurance company, whereby the use of legal German has been fairly advantagous. 

The overall motivation was also personal, as I have family in Germany. I wanted to experience the amazing city and make friends from Germany.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it very difficult. The organisational structure was chaotic, and mostly just me asking my fellow German and international students for guidance. It could've been better and the only way I received answers was per e-mail, weeks after I needed the answer. The physical Büro was not open, and the number linked to our guidance - was nonexistent.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was one introductory lecturer that - bear in mind, only in German - introduced an hour long of formal information, that we were expected to just sort out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was incredibly difficult. Housing in Berlin is very in-demand, so I joined several Facebook groups, wrote contacts and ended up finding a private dorm called Neon Wood. It was rather expensive, but it was in the heart of Berlin.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's better than Adlershof... but it is expensive. You pay for the location and the private kitchen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was along the lines of trying about every course for the first week, and then deciding what courses you like. It was chaotic at first, as it differed from what we were used to, and it was explained poorly. The idea/concept in itself is however great. You get to see what courses actually interest you, and how the professors are!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Internationales Prüfungsbüro.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesfull. I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun, and don't stress all too much about all the formalities. Ask the German students, they know more than the actual teachers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the difficulty to vary a fair bit from course to course. Overall it was very interesting, and a different teaching form than what I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It simply meant there was a lot less group work, and it was dominated by lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Copyright law, Patentrecht, FRS - American Constitutional Law, MEUC, Einführung und Allgemeiner Teil des StGB and English Legal System.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
FRS - American Constitutional Law was incredibly immersive. It was very American in its style of teaching (pop quizzes each week, midterms and finals), but you really learned a lot! 

MEUC - Model European Union Conference, was very interesting. You get to pretend to sit in the EU parlament, and represent a country.

questions.answer: Entrance fee to clubs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food due to inflation!! It is still cheaper than Copenhagen, but it definitely isn't as cheap as it used to be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't personally partake in any, but there were plenty of sports clubs!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The food, clubbing and the nightlife. They are iconic in Berlin and should definitely be explored.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the museums, Mauerpark, the bar scene, local restaurants...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak German to them! Tell them that you are an Erasmus student and want to get to know their culture!!!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. At times it was tiresome and difficult to hold a conversation in German

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness from everyone!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You can do it (you'll manage with the German), go to the events on campus and meet up with the local students and don't forget to bring cash!!!! (They don't take credit card most places)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to have fun, don't spend all your time in the library or on campus. Meet locals from other humanities/sciences/universities! Explore, explore, explore.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and having made incredible friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and the closed book exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
